start.text: An old woman in waxed leathers mends an eel-trap outside a stilt-hut. "Mind where you put your boots, dryfoot. The fen's been eating better than usual lately."

choices.label: What do you mean, eating better?
Three lights snuffed. Cold as coins, these motes.

lights.text: "Lights. Pale blue, bobbing sweet as a lantern on a friend's arm - out where there's no path and no friend. Tinker followed one Tuesday last. Found his hat." She ties off a knot. "Snuff three of them and bring me the cold that's left behind. I'll pay. The fen and I have an arrangement, and they're spoiling it."

lights_done.text: She weighs the motes in her palm like a fishmonger. "Cold and honest. The causeway'll be safe for a season, maybe two." She counts coins out of a tin that smells of eels. "The fen thanks you, in its way. You'll know its way when your boots stay dry."

text: "Chapel, west and north. Quiet Light folk built it, back when. Bell's been ringing with no hand on the rope, and I don't ferry that way anymore."
"The shamblers? Peat and old drowned things. Slow as debt. Don't let them corner you against the water - they don't tire and you do."
"Bramblewick's mine went quiet, I heard. The ground here heard it too. Some nights the fen-water shivers in rings, all pointing east."
